latestFinding.reason: On forced Adapter drop, the parent kills and waits for the Python child. The Job is subsequently closed, triggering kill-on-close for assigned browser descendants, but the ordinary path does not obtain positive zero-active-process accounting before releasing its browser-session lock. Job::wait_empty and terminate_and_wait_empty exist but are not used by this ordinary teardown path. The source therefore does not prove descendant quiescence before another owner can acquire the lock.
latestFinding.qualification: This is a concrete missing lifecycle proof, not evidence that a duplicate USER submission occurred. The delivery witness and SUBMITTING no-replay protections remain separate. Whether actual browser-profile overlap occurs requires further qualification.

confirmedCurrentSourceGap: Adapter Drop waited for Python only. The retained private Job was closed asynchronously without positive zero-active-process accounting before the browser lock field dropped. Ordinary retirement and outer callers supplied no later wait barrier.
